newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cen bank seeks policy mix, not lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cen bank seeks policy mix, not lower rates.

text.p: Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Monday he believes Europe's economies need a better policy mix rather than lower interest rates.

"A better policy mix is better than reducing already very low interest rates," Verplaetse told Reuters by telephone. He was asked to comment on an interview in Friday's Luxemburger Wort newspaper which quoted Verplaetse as saying interest rates should not be cut to stimulate Europe's economy.
"No, that would be stupid. I am of the opinion that interest rates are low enough. What Europe needs more is a better policy mix," Verplaetse was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
The interview took place last Thursday.
"I said that in the past budgetary policies were lax and the job had to be done by monetary policy. I said that was not good. I prefer orthodox budgetary policies," Verplaetse told Reuters.

"I am not saying that the mix at the moment is bad...for the time being it's O.K.. In most countries, budgets are coming under control and this gives more leeway for monetary policy," Verplaetse added.
The Luxemburger Wort quoted Verplaetse as saying cutting interest rates further would not serve any purpose.
"Take the example of Japan, they have had very low interest rates for some time, but the economy still has not picked up speed," the newspaper quoted Verplaetse as saying.
